description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of entity types identified by a biomedical named entity recognition system, with the largest segment being "Protein" at 32%, followed by "Drug" at 4%, "Cell Type" at 5%, "Disease" at 5%, "Chemical Family" at 5%, "DNA" at 6%, and "Protein" at 15%. The remaining categories, including "Gene Or Gene Product," "Form," "Strength," "Dosage," "Cell Line," "Frequency," "Route," "Reason," "Specific Disease," "Disease Or Phenotypic Feature," "Chemical Entity," "Sequence Variant," "Modifier," "RNA," "Disease Class," "Organism Taxon," "Duration," and "Composite Mention," each constitute 1% or 2% of the total. The chart is divided into 18 distinct slices, each labeled with its corresponding entity type and percentage value, with no visual emphasis such as exploded slices or bolding. The segments appear to be arranged in descending order of size from the largest to smallest, starting with Protein and ending with the smallest categories.
